key_insight: The paper introduces a 3D CFD-DDA framework showing that UV light scattering inside airborne saliva droplets is highly non-uniform and materially changes predicted virus inactivation.
engineering_relevance: This improves the physics basis for designing and optimizing UV air purification systems by accounting for droplet evaporation, transport, wall effects, and scattering-driven shielding.
method: Coupled CFD droplet transport/evaporation with DDA-based UV scattering in a fully three-dimensional Euler–Lagrange framework.
Simulated spherical and evaporation-deformed saliva droplets containing virus under airflow and UV irradiation.
Derived a new Dbouk-Yurkin inactivation law that extends Chick-Watson to include scattering effects.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports model-based evaluation of surviving coronavirus copies Ns across droplet size distributions, airflow rates, and droplet-wall interactions at 21 °C and 65% relative humidity.
watch_item: The conclusions depend on model assumptions for virion size, droplet properties, and UV-scattering physics, so experimental validation would be important before deployment.
paper_title: An Innovative Computational Fluid Dynamics Discrete Dipole Approximation (CFD-DDA) Platform for Predicting Airborne Virus-in-Saliva Disinfection by Ultraviolet Irradiation
